'''Bitcoin Gold''' ('''BTG''') is a [[cryptocurrency]] which was created as a [[Fork_(blockchain)#Hard_fork|hard fork]] of [[bitcoin]].

The stated purpose of the hard fork is to make [[Cryptocurrency#Mining|mining]] on commonly available graphics cards economically viable. The cryptocurrency has been hit by two [[Double-spending#51% attack|51% hashing attack]]s, once in 2018 and once in 2020.

== History ==

Bitcoin Gold [[Fork_(blockchain)#Hard_fork|hard forked]] from the bitcoin blockchain on October 24, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/a-new-bitcoin-fork-looms-to-create-bitcoin-gold-trading/|title=New, imminent Bitcoin Gold fork met with skepticism|last=Osborne|first=Charlie|website=ZDNet|language=en|access-date=2019-01-16|archive-date=2017-10-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024235403/https://www.zdnet.com/article/a-new-bitcoin-fork-looms-to-create-bitcoin-gold-trading/|url-status=live}}</ref> The stated purpose of the hard fork was to change the [[proof of work]] [[algorithm]] so that ASICs ([[Application-specific integrated circuit|Application-Specific Integrated Circuits]]) which are used to mine bitcoin cannot be used to mine the Bitcoin Gold [[blockchain]] in the hopes that enabling mining on commonly available graphics cards would allow mining from a home PC.<ref name=Fortune>{{Cite web|url=http://fortune.com/2017/10/25/bitcoin-gold-fork-cash/|title=Meet Bitcoin Gold, Yet Another New Kind of Bitcoin|website=Fortune|language=en|access-date=2019-01-16|archive-date=2017-10-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171025153024/http://fortune.com/2017/10/25/bitcoin-gold-fork-cash/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=mashable>{{Cite web|url=https://mashable.com/2017/10/24/bitcoin-fork-bitcoin-gold/|title=Bitcoin splits into two again, but owners don't get free money just yet|last=Schroeder|first=Stan|website=Mashable|date=24 October 2017|language=en|access-date=2019-01-16|archive-date=2017-10-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024161845/https://mashable.com/2017/10/24/bitcoin-fork-bitcoin-gold/|url-status=live}}</ref>

According to [[Mashable]] the launch was criticized for being hastily put together and for including a developer pre-mine.<ref name=mashable/> Shortly after launch, the project's website came under a [[distributed denial of service attack]].<ref name=Fortune/>

In May 2018, Bitcoin Gold was hit by a [[Double-spending#51% attack|51% hashing attack]] by an unknown actor. This type of attack makes it possible to manipulate the blockchain ledger on which transactions are recorded, and to spend the same digital coins more than once.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fortune.com/2018/05/29/bitcoin-gold-hack/|title=Bitcoin Spinoff Hacked in Rare '51% Attack'|website=Fortune|language=en|access-date=2019-01-16|archive-date=2019-01-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190116061454/http://fortune.com/2018/05/29/bitcoin-gold-hack/|url-status=dead}}</ref> During the attack, 388,000 BTG (worth approximately US$18 million) was stolen from several cryptocurrency exchanges. Bitcoin Gold was later delisted from Bittrex, after the team refused to help pay some damages.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/bitcoin-gold-delisted-from-major-cryptocurrency-exchange-after-refusing-to-pay-hack-damages/|title=Bitcoin Gold delisted from major cryptocurrency exchange after refusing to pay hack damages|last=Cimpanu|first=Catalin|website=ZDNet|language=en|access-date=2019-01-16|archive-date=2022-05-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220524122220/https://www.zdnet.com/article/bitcoin-gold-delisted-from-major-cryptocurrency-exchange-after-refusing-to-pay-hack-damages/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In July 2018, Bitcoin Gold changed mining algorithm to one that requires more memory to further discourage ASIC mining.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Iskra|first1=Edward|title=Equihash-BTG: Our New PoW Algorithm|url=https://btgofficial.org/equihash-btg/|access-date=21 June 2019|website=Bitcoin Gold|archive-date=16 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250116212839/https://btgofficial.org/equihash-btg/|url-status=live}}</ref>{{primary inline|date=September 2024}}

Bitcoin Gold suffered from 51% attacks again in January 2020.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Canellis |first1=David |title=Bitcoin Gold hit by 51% attacks, $72K in cryptocurrency double-spent |url=https://thenextweb.com/hardfork/2020/01/27/bitcoin-gold-51-percent-attack-blockchain-reorg-cryptocurrency-binance-exchange/ |website=The Next Web |date=January 27, 2020 |access-date=February 27, 2020 |archive-date=January 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200127152040/https://thenextweb.com/hardfork/2020/01/27/bitcoin-gold-51-percent-attack-blockchain-reorg-cryptocurrency-binance-exchange/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In July 2020, the version 0.17.2 was released as an emergency update in order to elude a long attack chain originated a few days before.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://btgofficial.org/emergency-update-0-17-2/|website=Bitcoin Gold|title=Emergency update 0.17.2|access-date=4 Sep 2020|archive-date=1 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240901140236/https://btgofficial.org/emergency-update-0-17-2/|url-status=live}}</ref>
